name: LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Y WITH ACUTE
reason: Acute accent on Latin Y; lowercase ý maps y and canonical decomposition is Y + acute.

name: LATIN CAPITAL LETTER D WITH SMALL LETTER Z
reason: Titlecase DZ digraph decomposes to D z; mapping drops z.

name: MODIFIER LETTER SMALL H
reason: Modifier small h has compatibility decomposition h, not k.

name: GREEK LUNATE SIGMA SYMBOL
reason: Lunate sigma is sigma, not Latin c; ALA-LC explicitly maps ϲ to s.

name: CYRILLIC CAPITAL LETTER IE WITH GRAVE
proposed: E (Je if choosing a je convention)
reason: This is Е with grave, not Ё/IO; Jo substitutes an o vowel. Ordinary Е maps E. Lowercase ѐ maps je, so case pair also disagrees.

name: BENGALI LETTER VOCALIC L
reason: Bengali VOCALIC L belongs to vocalic l series, not vocalic RR; dependent counterpart U+09E2 maps L.

name: BENGALI LETTER RA WITH LOWER DIAGONAL
reason: Despite misleading Unicode formal name RA WITH LOWER DIAGONAL, Unicode identifies this as Assamese wa; r` is the wrong consonant.

name: GURMUKHI LETTER BHA
reason: Gurmukhi BHA is bha in ALA-LC, consonantal skeleton bh; bb is not the corresponding consonant.

name: THAI CHARACTER SO SO
reason: Thai SO SO is s initially, t finally; ch is not either reading.

name: THAI CHARACTER LAKKHANGYAO
reason: Lakkhangyao lengthens ฤ or ฦ; ao introduces an unrelated o. Unicode calls it a vowel length sign; a correct readable result requires context.

name: LAO LETTER TO
reason: Lao TO is t, not h; ALA-LC uses t both initially and finally.

name: LAO LETTER HO TAM
reason: Lao HO TAM is h initially. Empty string erases an ordinary consonant.

name: ARABIC LETTER JEH
reason: Persian/Pashto JEH is zh, not j; distinct from Arabic JEEM which maps j.

name: ARABIC LETTER KEHEH
reason: Persian/Urdu keheh is k, not kh; LoC Persian note 2 explicitly shows ک as kaf form.

name: ARABIC LETTER E
reason: Pashto vowel E is romanized e. Empty string deletes a written vowel.

name: ARABIC LETTER HAH WITH THREE DOTS ABOVE
reason: Pashto letter TSE is represented by ALA-LC ṡ; ts/s depend on dialect. H is not either consonant.

name: ARABIC LETTER KAF WITH RING
reason: Pashto ګ is g in the ALA-LC alphabet; the data uses K.

name: HEBREW LIGATURE YIDDISH DOUBLE YOD
reason: Yiddish double yod represents ey/ay, not i; LoC explicitly lists both diphthongs. Prefer ey as unpointed YIVO default, with ay requiring context/pointing.

name: GREEK SMALL LETTER IOTA WITH DIALYTIKA AND TONOS
reason: Lowercase Greek iota with dialytika and tonos is currently uppercase I, while other lowercase iotas map i.

name: CYRILLIC CAPITAL LETTER UK
reason: Capital Cyrillic UK maps lowercase u, while lowercase U+0479 also maps u; restore the capital U.

name: CYRILLIC CAPITAL LETTER A WITH BREVE
reason: Capital Cyrillic A with breve maps lowercase a; lowercase U+04D1 maps a.

name: GREEK CAPITAL LETTER UPSILON WITH TONOS
reason: Capital upsilon with tonos uses U while unaccented Υ and lowercase ύ use Y/y. U can occur in classical romanization, so this is scheme/case consistency, not universally an impossible reading.

name: LATIN CAPITAL LETTER UPSILON
reason: Latin capital upsilon maps Y although its lowercase ʊ maps U (SAMPA-style). Unlike Greek upsilon, this is a Latin IPA/orthographic letter. Needs policy review.

name: GUJARATI LETTER YA
reason: Gujarati YA uniquely includes inherent a (ya), while neighboring consonants are bare and dependent vowels append, producing duplicate/inappropriate a before explicit vowel signs. Isolated ya itself is a valid romanization.

name: GURMUKHI ADDAK
reason: Gurmukhi addak/adhik marks gemination; fixed H inserts unrelated h. ALA-LC specifies doubling the following consonant.

name: ARABIC SHADDA
reason: Arabic shadda marks gemination; fixed W inserts unrelated w. ALA-LC Persian/Pashto specifies doubling the letter/digraph.

name: ORIYA LETTER VA
reason: Odia VA is a consonant, not an ignorable sign; data currently drops it. Primary Unicode identity supports nonempty consonantal fallback; preferred scheme needs specialist confirmation.

name: DEVANAGARI LETTER DDDHA
reason: Devanagari DDDHA is the flap ṛ (ड़), not an aspirated dddh sequence. Existing data RRA uses rr. Hindi chart retrieval not yet verified; ask language reviewer.
